title: Ticket export with every attribute
prompt: The ticketing tool takes one row per log record, with all of the record's attributes as a single JSON text field, whatever keys they hold. The starter saves the log file; finish `solve(application_logs_raw)` to build that export from the good records.
rules: Return `log_id`, `logged_at` (a timestamp), `level`, `service` and `attributes_json`, in that order.

`attributes_json` is the record's whole `attributes` object as JSON text, every key in the order it arrived, for example `{"host":"auth-service-a41d8","region":"us-east"}`. No attributes gives NULL; an empty object gives `{}`.
Leave out lines that aren't valid JSON, and records whose `logged_at` isn't a valid timestamp.
hints: The keys change from record to record, so a struct with fixed fields won't do. A map has no fixed keys: `attributes MAP<STRING,STRING>` in the schema.
`F.to_json(...)` turns a map column into JSON text.
Put `logged_at TIMESTAMP` in the schema so a bad time counts as malformed, and choose the mode that leaves malformed records out.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(application_logs_raw):
    path = "/tmp/logs/export"
    application_logs_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    # Read the file at `path` and return the ticket export.
    return application_logs_raw
explanation: Read `attributes` as a map, because its keys differ from line to line: `spark.read.json(path, schema="log_id STRING, logged_at TIMESTAMP, level STRING, service STRING, attributes MAP<STRING,STRING>", mode="DROPMALFORMED")`. Then `F.to_json("attributes").alias("attributes_json")` writes each map back as text with its keys in their original order. With `logged_at` typed as a timestamp in the schema, a record whose time doesn't parse is malformed, so `DROPMALFORMED` leaves it out along with the broken lines. A struct schema would only keep the keys you list, and letting Spark infer the schema would merge every key it has seen into one struct, sorted by name, and read `logged_at` as text.
